clue.text: 4's shoe

definitions.meaning: the 4-down answer: a cold-blooded scaly creature, here the water snake of the American south
a soft leather slip-on with no heel, of Native American origin

explanation.surface: A question of what footwear some creature wears.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to the answer at 4-down, the theme of the puzzle; the 's simply joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The water snake of the American south and a soft heelless leather slip-on share one name.

clue.text: Time to manoeuvre to gain entry

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to shift into new positions, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Timing a manoeuvre to get in somewhere, like a burglar or a driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Each separate entry in a list or catalogue is called an item.

clue.text: Personal cover generous? Not right, so brave to be under it?

parts.note: a wig covers a person's head

explanation.surface: Asking whether a generous hairpiece is the sort of thing a brave would shelter under.
explanation.walkthrough: A brave is a Native American warrior, so the tent he lives under is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed tent dwelling of some Native American peoples, so a warrior would sleep beneath one.

clue.text: Penny goes in to renovate bathroom scales on one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bathroom scales' looks like a single object, but 'scales' belongs with the definition: a creature with scales on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes, lizards and their kin are covered in horny scales, so this describes such a creature.

clue.text: Morality play for himself?

parts.note: names a famous medieval English morality play whose title also begins the saying about each person looking after only his own interests

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a moral drama is being staged for one person.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifteenth-century morality play bears this title, and the idiom about selfishness begins with the same words.

clue.text: Failing prison also for godparents

indicators.note: failing means falling apart, so the letters of the words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sponsors at a christening also failing and ending up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Godparents are sponsors at a baptism, so an adjective relating to sponsors fits.

clue.text: Defeated by gun just loaded

definitions.meaning: beaten, crushed in spirit or overcome
a shotgun is snapped open at the hinge to load it

explanation.surface: Someone beaten by a gun that has just been loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeated person is crushed, and a shotgun is opened at its hinge for loading.

clue.text: 4's wrong sound with head tucked away

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is hidden from view, like a head drawn into a shell

parts.note: a noise is a sound

explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to the answer at 4-down; the 's reads as 'is'. The head tucked in is exactly what this slow creature does.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow land-dwelling creature with a shell, which is one kind of cold-blooded scaly animal.

clue.text: 4 takes some of its letters and its number back

indicators.note: back says the two pieces together are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the first three letters of the 4-down answer
the clue number of 4-down, written in Roman numerals

explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake, such as the adder, is a member of the cold-blooded scaly class of animals.

clue.text: Useless film where group of rugby players run away

indicators.note: run away says the letter for run leaves the word

parts.note: a scrum is a set formation of rugby forwards

explanation.surface: A bad film in which the rugby pack runs off the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests cinema, but it is a thin layer on the surface of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer of dirt or froth forming on a liquid's surface is worthless matter.

clue.text: 4 writhing astern in trail of boat

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A snake that lives in or near water is one kind of cold-blooded scaly creature.

clue.text: Might those seeking this have a problem accommodating "Daily Mail's conclusions", ultimately?

definitions.text: Might those seeking this have a problem accommodating "Daily Mail's conclusions", ultimately?

indicators.note: accommodating means taking in, so the last letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: the conclusions of the two words are their final letters

explanation.surface: A dig at a newspaper's hostile coverage of refugees.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: refugees seeking it might well have trouble with that newspaper's views. 'ultimately' just reinforces 'conclusions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Refugees seek protection in another country, so the clue as a whole describes that protection.

clue.text: Close game which is different or called "close"

parts.note: by means near, close at hand

explanation.surface: A tight match, played differently or labelled near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' in the definition means local, not tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A match between neighbouring rival teams is a game between close rivals.

clue.text: Satirical pieces producing whack on nose sent back

parts.note: to nose around is to snoop

explanation.surface: Satirical pieces that amount to a punch on the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the reversed piece after LAM. 'nose' is a verb here, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Satirical sketches or writings that mock their subjects.

clue.text: Horny beast imagined finding garment ripped, models having fled

ripped means torn
the Model T was Ford's early car, so models are Ts

pro means for

clue.text: Neighbour to stroke cow is an eccentric accepting kiss

eccentric means odd, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: In a rowing eight the steersman sits at the stern, right next to the stroke oarsman.

clue.text: Swimmer stuffing non-starter — much left!

clue.text: Disheartened male or female going round shops and post office, appearing rash?

disheartened says the middle letter is removed

explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like an adjective, but it is the skin eruption of the disease.
